rationale: SnackLoop is a direct-to-consumer snack subscription service targeted at busy families. It fits squarely within our Consumer CPG thesis, with individual consumers acting as both the end users and the paying customers.

GlowNest is a direct-to-consumer skincare membership brand offering recurring product refills, aligning perfectly with our Consumer CPG thesis. The primary end user and paying customer is the individual consumer making personal purchasing decisions.

FitJournal is a direct-to-consumer fitness tracking app that allows individuals to monitor wellness goals. It fits perfectly into our Consumer Health Tech thesis with an individual consumer as the target user.

CalmRoute is a direct-to-consumer meditation and sleep coaching app, aligning perfectly with our consumer health tech thesis. It operates directly in the wellness industry for individual consumers with no B2B or employer-funded distribution indicators.

TripMint is a direct-to-consumer travel booking app focusing on weekend getaways and vacation planning, which is a strong fit for our consumer travel & hospitality thesis. The primary user is an individual consumer making personal travel decisions.

DineDesk is a restaurant reservation app designed for individual diners to discover local restaurants. It fits our thesis perfectly by operating in the hospitality sector for consumers, acting as a consumer-facing discovery tool and marketplace.

HomeHaul is a direct-to-consumer marketplace for secondhand home decor and furniture. It perfectly aligns with our focus on consumer-facing two-sided markets where the primary transaction and decision-maker is an individual consumer.

PetPantry is a grocery and meal planning app for pet owners, making it a strong consumer pet tech play. Since the end user and paying customer is the individual pet owner making direct personal purchase decisions, it avoids B2B-in-disguise traps and fits well within our thesis.

TrailTaste is a direct-to-consumer beverage and nutrition brand designed specifically for hikers. This aligns perfectly with our Consumer CPG thesis, targeting individual outdoor enthusiasts with direct-to-consumer food and beverage options.

GuestJoy is a consumer-facing mobile app that allows travelers to book boutique hotel stays and experiences directly. It operates in the travel and hospitality sector for individual consumers, aligning well with our investment thesis.
PipelinePilot provides workflow automation software for sales teams and revenue operations. This is a pure B2B SaaS product, which is explicitly excluded from our consumer investment thesis.

DevTrace is an API observability platform for engineering teams, classifying it as a B2B developer tool. Developer tools and infrastructure are explicitly excluded from our consumer-focused investment thesis.
CloudLedger is an ERP and payroll platform designed for finance departments. It is a pure B2B enterprise software solution, which is explicitly excluded from our investment thesis.

InfraMint provides Kubernetes infrastructure tooling for platform engineers. Since it is a developer tool and enterprise infrastructure product, it is explicitly excluded from our consumer-focused investment thesis.

ConsultForge is a professional services agency building analytics dashboards for enterprises. This is a B2B service/consulting business, which is strictly excluded from our investment thesis targeting early-stage consumer startups.

RetailOpsOS is a B2B SaaS platform that sells inventory and staffing tools directly to retail businesses. Because its paying customers and end users are businesses rather than individual consumers, it falls outside our consumer investment thesis.

GuestStack is an enterprise property management software designed for hotel chains. Because it sells software tools directly to businesses in the hospitality industry rather than serving individual consumers, it is excluded from our consumer investment thesis.

HealthSwitch is an enterprise B2B SaaS analytics platform for HR teams to manage benefits spend. It sells tools directly to businesses and has no direct-to-consumer component, putting it outside of our investment thesis.

MerchantMesh is a B2B marketplace infrastructure provider for wholesalers and retail sellers. It is excluded from our thesis because it sells enterprise software and tools to businesses rather than targeting individual consumers.

ChainSignal is a blockchain analytics product for token compliance teams. It falls under the crypto and B2B enterprise software categories, both of which are explicitly excluded from our consumer investment thesis.

TableVoice is an enterprise API platform designed for restaurants to handle AI voice ordering. Since it sells software tools to businesses in the restaurant industry rather than serving individual consumers directly, it is classified as B2B SaaS and falls outside our consumer thesis.

HotelCore is a property management system for hotels, which is a B2B SaaS product. Our thesis excludes enterprise software and tools sold to industries, focusing instead on direct-to-consumer and consumer marketplace models.

ShelfMind is a B2B enterprise software company selling merchandising analytics tools directly to grocery retailers. Because the paying customer and end users are businesses rather than individual consumers, it does not fit our consumer-focused investment thesis.

MenuMatrix is a B2B SaaS reservation CRM sold directly to restaurants. Because it sells software tools to the industry rather than operating as a consumer-facing service, it falls outside our consumer investment thesis.

TravelConsole is a backend booking API designed for travel agencies and hotel operators. As a developer tool and B2B infrastructure provider, it falls outside of our consumer-focused investment thesis.

DinerFlow is a B2B SaaS operating system sold directly to restaurants. Because the paying customer is a business and the product is an operational tool rather than a consumer-facing application or marketplace, it is excluded from our consumer thesis.

CheckInPilot is a guest messaging and upsell platform designed for hotel front desks, making it a B2B SaaS tool sold to hotels rather than a consumer-facing travel or hospitality product. Since the paying customer and primary end-users are businesses, it is excluded from our consumer thesis.

ClinicCart is a B2B white-label SaaS platform selling nutrition ordering tools to health clinics. Since the paying customer is a business (the clinic) and it sells operating tools to the industry rather than directly to consumers, it is excluded from our consumer-focused thesis.

TourStack provides booking APIs and back-office software directly to tour operators. Because it sells developer tools and enterprise software to businesses rather than operating a consumer-facing platform, it is excluded from our consumer investment thesis.

MemberBowl is a B2B loyalty CRM sold directly to restaurant franchise chains. Because it sells software tools to businesses in the hospitality industry rather than operating a consumer-facing platform or marketplace, it is excluded from our consumer investment thesis.

FamilyFareOS is a B2B SaaS platform licensed by school districts. Since the paying customer is an institution rather than an individual consumer making a personal purchase decision, this falls outside our consumer investment thesis.

AdTunes is a consumer-facing music discovery app that operates as a two-sided marketplace. Although it monetizes via business advertisers, the primary end user is an individual consumer using the product for personal entertainment, making it a good fit for our consumer thesis.

ReadFree is a consumer-facing reading app for students. While the paying customers are brand advertisers, the platform operates directly in the consumer space where individual users make personal decisions to engage with the content, making it a good fit for our consumer thesis.

StreamPerks is a direct-to-consumer entertainment application featuring an ad-supported premium subscription model, aligning well with our consumer focus. It serves individual consumers directly without B2B distribution complexities.

NewsNest is a consumer-facing local news digest app that operates in the media space for individual consumers. However, because it relies on ad/sponsor monetization and does not fall within our core focus areas of CPG, Health Tech, Travel, or Marketplaces, it represents a marginal thesis match.

While the end-user is an individual consumer, the startup monetizes by selling sponsorships to tourism boards. This B2B/B2G revenue model diverges from our consumer thesis which focuses on direct consumer purchases.

StudySnack is a direct-to-consumer budget meal-planning utility app for college students. While monetized via CPG brand advertising, the primary end user is an individual consumer making personal daily decisions, aligning well with our consumer thesis.

PlayPassFree is a direct-to-consumer casual gaming and rewards app. It targets individual consumers directly, aligning with our consumer focus, although its ad-based monetization model relies on business advertisers as the paying customers.

WellBenefit is an employer-sponsored wellness app where the paying customer is the employer and there is no evidence of a direct-to-consumer acquisition channel. Under our thesis rules, employer-funded wellness programs are classified as B2B-in-disguise and scored in the review flag range.

MindStipend is an employer-funded mental health app. Since the paying customer is the business (employer) and it is distributed as a workplace benefit, it falls under our employer-funded distribution rule and is flagged for human review.

BenefitPath is a care-navigation app distributed through employer benefit programs. Since the paying customer is a business and there is no evidence of a direct-to-consumer channel, it is flagged as an ambiguous employer-funded model.

RecoverCircle is a musculoskeletal recovery app offered through employers and health plans. Because it relies on employer-funded distribution without evidence of a direct-to-consumer channel, it is classified as a B2B-in-disguise benefit program and scored low for human review.

FamilyFuel is a fertility and family planning app bundled into employer benefits packages. Because the paying customer is the employer with no evidence of an independent D2C channel, this falls under the employer-funded benefits distribution rule and is scored low to flag for manual review.

CareBridge Home is a family caregiving coordination app distributed via employee support stipends. Because it relies on employer-funded distribution and benefits packages without clear evidence of a direct-to-consumer acquisition channel, it is flagged for human review under our employer-benefits rule.

ShiftCalm is a stress management app distributed as an hourly-worker benefit. Because the paying customer is the employer and there is no independent D2C channel mentioned, it falls under the employer-funded distribution rule.

LocalTable is a two-sided marketplace connecting diners with restaurants for reservations. It fits our thesis perfectly as it operates in the hospitality sector for individual consumers rather than selling enterprise software to restaurants.

StaySwap is a two-sided consumer marketplace for vacation home rentals. The primary end user and paying customer are individual consumers booking travel accommodations, making this a strong fit for our consumer marketplace and travel thesis.

GearLoop operates a peer-to-peer consumer marketplace for renting outdoor gear, matching individuals who want to rent gear with local owners. The end-user and paying customer are both individual consumers, aligning directly with our thesis on consumer-facing marketplaces.

MealMeet is a direct consumer-facing marketplace matching individual office workers with home chefs for lunch orders. The end user is an individual consumer making a personal purchase decision, which aligns directly with our consumer marketplace and FoodTech thesis.

PupStay is a peer-to-peer consumer marketplace matching pet owners with local pet sitters. It directly serves individual consumers who make personal purchase decisions, making it a strong fit for our consumer marketplace thesis.

TripTrade is a peer-to-peer marketplace allowing individual travelers to trade unused travel perks and activity credits. It fits cleanly into our consumer marketplace and travel/hospitality theses, focusing entirely on direct consumer-to-consumer transactions.

LessonLane is a consumer-facing marketplace connecting parents with local instructors for extracurricular classes. It aligns perfectly with our investment thesis as a consumer marketplace where the primary end user and paying customer is the individual consumer making personal purchasing decisions.

ShiftSnack is a consumer marketplace that helps gig workers find discounted meals. Because the end user is an individual consumer making direct personal purchase decisions, this falls clearly within our thesis and avoids any B2B/employer-funded GTM concerns.

DriverRecover is a mobile wellness app designed for rideshare drivers to manage sleep, stress, and exercise. Since it is purchased directly by individual gig workers rather than distributed as an employer-funded benefit, it is a strong fit for our consumer health tech thesis.

CourierCover offers insurance and care directly to independent couriers. However, insurance and benefits infrastructure for gig workers straddles the boundary between services and health tech, which triggers a manual review flag according to our thesis guidelines.

RouteRelief is an expense-tracking and mental wellness app purchased directly by individual delivery drivers to manage fuel and burnout. Because it targets gig workers directly as individual consumers rather than through an employer benefit package, it fits our consumer health tech and wellness thesis.

TaskShield provides portable accident coverage for gig workers. Although purchased directly by individual consumers, insurance and benefits-infrastructure products for gig workers are excluded or flagged as ambiguous due to straddling the services and health-tech boundary.

RunnerMeals offers a direct-to-consumer meal subscription service tailored for gig workers. Since the individual workers are the primary end users making personal purchase decisions rather than the platforms funding it, this is a strong fit for our consumer food/CPG thesis.

SoloCreator operates as a creator economy platform facilitating fan memberships and content drops. Since it serves individual creators and their fans directly rather than B2B brands, it fits our criteria for consumer-facing creator monetization tools.

BrandBriefly is a workflow SaaS tool built for enterprise marketing teams to hire influencers. This is a B2B software product, which is explicitly excluded from our consumer-focused investment thesis.

CraftLaunch is a consumer-facing creator economy platform allowing individual creators to sell digital products directly to fans. It matches our thesis as a consumer-facing two-sided marketplace where the end transactions are driven by individual consumer purchase decisions.

FanRoster fits our creator economy thesis as a consumer-facing monetization tool that allows individual podcasters to run paid fan clubs. The primary paying customer is the individual consumer purchasing access, making this an eligible consumer marketplace.

CollabLedger is a B2B SaaS platform offering contract and payment operations software for talent agencies. Because the product is sold directly to agencies rather than individual creators or everyday consumers, it falls outside of our consumer investment thesis.

ClipCart operates as a consumer-facing creator economy platform, allowing individual video creators to sell digital bundles directly to their followers. This falls under our thesis as it focuses on monetization tools for individual creators rather than B2B SaaS for brands.
